title: Protect cc pin against renovate lock file maintenance
body:

List any relevant issue numbers:

- resolves none; related: rust-lang/cc-rs#1940, #6520

### Description

This makes the `cc` 1.4.6 / `find-msvc-tools` 0.1.12 pins from #6520 durable against renovate updates.

`cc` 1.4.7 changes the clang `--target` triple passed for `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` to `arm-unknown-linux-gnueabihf`, which breaks the `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` CI build (upstream report: rust-lang/cc-rs#1940). #6520 fixed the build by pinning `cc` back to 1.4.6 in `Cargo.lock` only — but renovate's weekly lock file maintenance runs a wholesale `cargo update` and does not apply `allowedVersions` package rules to lock-only entries. This is not hypothetical: the existing `stacker` rule (`allowedVersions: "<=0.1.23"`) was bypassed by lock file maintenance in #6471 and stacker is at 0.1.25 today. So without this change, the next lock file maintenance PR reverts the `cc` pin and turns the armv7 build red again.

Therefore:

- `cc = "=1.4.6"` and `find-msvc-tools = "=0.1.12"` are added as explicit `[build-dependencies]` of `bindings_napi`, the crate whose `libmimalloc-sys2` → `cmake` → `cc` build chain is affected. Cargo version unification keeps the whole workspace on these versions, and `cargo update` cannot bump past an `=` requirement. Both crates are already compiled on every platform as part of that chain, so this adds no build cost.
- Matching `allowedVersions` renovate rules are added so renovate does not open PRs that update the pin entries themselves.

No new tests: the `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf` CI job is the regression test — it failed with `cc` 1.4.7 (link failure in `libmimalloc-sys2`: `cannot open crtbeginS.o` / `-lgcc`) and passes with the pin, as verified in #6520. `cargo update --dry-run` now reports `cc` and `find-msvc-tools` as "unchanged" despite newer versions being available.

Both pins should be removed once rust-lang/cc-rs#1940 is fixed and a release without the regression is out.
